mainTopic: The minimum value for קידושין: בית שמאי's דינר, the fixed value of a פרוטה, and שמואל's concern about items worth less
overview: The גמרא finishes proving that an אמה העבריה must always be able to deduct from her price, so she can never be sold for one פרוטה. בית שמאי learn from this that a woman cannot be betrothed with a פרוטה, and the minimum is set at a דינר. רבא gives a different reason: Jewish women should not be treated like ownerless property. Then the גמרא turns to בית הלל's פרוטה. רב יוסף thinks it means any small amount, but אביי shows it has a fixed value. רב דימי reports one-eighth of an איסר and רבין reports one-sixth. רב דימי explains that both are right, because the copper איסר changed in price while the פרוטה stayed fixed against silver. Finally, שמואל rules that betrothal with a cheap date creates a doubtful קידושין, and the גמרא compares this with real cases of a bundle of rags and a blue stone.

steps.title: Deduction works like designation: a sale where it is impossible is no sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that deduction applies only when it happens to be possible. Just as a sale is invalid wherever יעוד is impossible, a sale is invalid wherever deduction is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be. Deduction is like designation. With designation, the master may designate her or not, as he chooses. Still, wherever designation is impossible, the sale is not a real sale. So too, wherever she cannot deduct from her price, the sale is not a real sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the earlier suggestion that an אמה העבריה deducts from her price only where possible. It says no: deduction must be possible, or the sale is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof compares deduction (גרעון) to יעוד. A master does not have to do יעוד, yet a sale where יעוד could never happen (for example, to a close relative) is not valid. In the same way, a sale where deduction could never happen, such as a sale for one פרוטה, is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; the idea is rejected
Designation: the master marries the אמה העבריה himself or gives her to his son as a wife
She deducts: she redeems herself by paying back part of her price
Sale

steps.confusionAlert: 'The master doesn't have to do it' is not the same as 'it doesn't matter if it's impossible.' An option the master may skip must still be possible in principle for the sale to work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that an אמה העבריה can never be sold for one פרוטה. בית שמאי build their view on קידושין on exactly this rule.

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind:
it is similar to designation.
Just as with designation,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִי בָּעֵי מְיַיעֵד
phrases.english: even though if he wants, he designates her,
and if he wants, he does not designate her,
anywhere that he cannot designate her,
her sale is not a valid sale,
so too, anywhere
that she cannot deduct from her price,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. Some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: her sale is not a valid sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ – דּוּמְיָא דְּיִיעוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier suggestion that deduction applies only where it happens to be possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Deduction is just a benefit that applies when possible; a sale where deduction is impossible could still be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Deduction must always be possible. A sale where it cannot happen, such as a sale for one פרוטה, is invalid, just like a sale where יעוד is impossible.

steps.title: בית שמאי learn קידושין from אמה העבריה
steps.stepSummary: According to בית שמאי, the rule for betrothing a woman with money comes from אמה העבריה. Since she cannot be acquired with a פרוטה, a woman cannot be betrothed with a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי learn betrothal of a woman from the Hebrew maidservant. Just as a Hebrew maidservant cannot be acquired with a פרוטה, a woman cannot be betrothed with a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies the rule from step 1 to קידושין, explaining where בית שמאי's view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that an אמה העבריה cannot be bought for a פרוטה, because she could not deduct from such a price. בית שמאי compare a woman's קידושין to this acquisition, so a פרוטה is not enough for קידושין either.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal of a woman
Hebrew maidservant: a young Jewish girl sold by her father
They derive it from
The smallest coin

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the long discussion of אמה העבריה back to the main question of the משנה: how much money is needed for קידושין.

phrases.english: And according to Beit Shammai, betrothal of a woman
is derived from the Hebrew maidservant:
just as a Hebrew maidservant
cannot be acquired with a peruta,
so too, a woman cannot be betrothed with a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִידּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָפְקָא לְהוּ מֵאָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the established rule about אמה העבריה to קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, a woman cannot be betrothed with a פרוטה, just as an אמה העבריה cannot be acquired with one.

steps.title: Why a whole דינר and not a smaller amount?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the comparison only rules out one פרוטה. Why not set the minimum at half a דינר, or even two פרוטות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say half a דינר? Or why not say two פרוטות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 2. The comparison only rules out a single פרוטה, so where does a full דינר come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה העבריה sold for two פרוטות could still deduct one פרוטה. So the derivation seems to prove only that more than one פרוטה is needed. A full דינר seems to go beyond what the source shows.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead; introduces a different possibility
Half a דינר
Two פרוטות

phrases.english: But say half a dinar,
or say two perutot!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא פַּלְגָא דְּדִינָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the amount that step 2 is meant to prove.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the אמה העבריה derivation supports a minimum of one דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The derivation rules out only one פרוטה, so any amount where deduction is possible, such as two פרוטות or half a דינר, should be enough.

steps.title: Once a פרוטה is ruled out, the amount is set at a דינר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that once the comparison takes קידושין away from a פרוטה, the amount is set at a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the comparison took her out of the פרוטה category, it set her at a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 3 with a short explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison shows that קידושין needs real, significant money rather than the smallest coin. Once the minimum is no longer a פרוטה, the next standard amount of real value is a דינר, so that is where it is set.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
It took her out of; it excluded
It set her; established her at

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית שמאי, the אמה העבריה comparison rules out a פרוטה, and the minimum for קידושין is then set at a full דינר.

phrases.english: Since it took her out of a peruta,
it established her at a dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאַפִּיקְתֵּיהּ מִפְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a set standard amount is chosen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any amount slightly above a פרוטה should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once a פרוטה is ruled out, the amount is set at the next real standard, a דינר.

steps.title: רבא: Jewish women should not be treated like ownerless property
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason for בית שמאי: betrothing a woman with just a פרוטה would make the daughters of Israel seem like הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is בית שמאי's reason: so that the daughters of Israel will not be like ownerless property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new explanation for בית שמאי that does not rely on the אמה העבריה comparison at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a source from the verses, רבא gives a reason based on respect. If a woman could be betrothed for the tiniest coin, it would look as if she were something cheap and available to anyone. Requiring a דינר protects her dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
The daughters of Israel; Jewish women
Ownerless property that anyone may take

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations for בית שמאי's דינר: a derivation from אמה העבריה, and רבא's reason that Jewish women should not be treated like הפקר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is the reason of Beit Shammai:
so that the daughters of Israel should not be like ownerless property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for בית שמאי's position instead of the derivation in steps 2 to 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require a דינר for קידושין so that Jewish women are not treated like ownerless property.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: בית הלל say a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: בית הלל hold that a woman can be betrothed with a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: with a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes with בית שמאי and now quotes בית הלל's side of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows about what exactly a פרוטה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי required a דינר. בית הלל set the minimum much lower, at a פרוטה. The next lines ask whether 'פרוטה' means a fixed amount or just any tiny coin.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, who argue with בית שמאי here
The smallest coin; the minimum value that counts as money in halacha

phrases.english: And בית הלל say: with a פרוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים בִּפְרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the explanation of בית שמאי's דינר to בית הלל's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, a woman can be betrothed with a פרוטה.

steps.title: רב יוסף thinks a פרוטה is any small amount
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף at first assumes that 'פרוטה' has no fixed value. It is whatever small coin people use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say: a פרוטה is any amount at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a first reading of בית הלל: a פרוטה is not a fixed measure. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יוסף is right, the smallest coin people use counts, whatever its real worth. The word 'סבר' warns us this is only a first thought, and it is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say; a first assumption that is usually rejected
Any amount at all, however small

phrases.english: רב יוסף thought to say:
A פרוטה is any amount at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term פרוטה used by בית הלל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: פרוטה has no fixed value.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה itself gives a fixed value
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. The same משנה defines a פרוטה as one-eighth of an Italian איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But it is taught right there about this: How much is a פרוטה? One-eighth of the Italian איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's idea by pointing to the משנה itself, which gives a set value for a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה bothers to say how much a פרוטה is, then a פרוטה cannot be 'any amount.' It is a fixed fraction of a known coin, the Italian איסר.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? This opens a challenge from a source
The Italian איסר, a Roman coin used to measure the פרוטה

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
But isn't it taught about this very ruling:
How much is a פרוטה?
One-eighth of the Italian איסר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְהָא עֲלַהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's assumption
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that a פרוטה is any amount
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה defines the פרוטה as a fixed fraction of the איסר, so it is not open-ended.

steps.title: Later sages also measured the פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks a possible answer. Someone might say the fixed value was only for the time of משה. But sages in later generations also measured the פרוטה as a fixed fraction of the איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: That was only in the generation of משה, but now it goes by what people consider a פרוטה. But when רב דימי came he said: רבי סימאי measured in his generation how much a פרוטה is: one-eighth of the Italian איסר. And when רבין came he said: רבי דוסתאי, רבי ינאי and רבי אושעיא measured how much a פרוטה is: one-sixth of the Italian איסר!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sees a way רב יוסף might answer and rejects it before he can say it. He proves that later sages also gave the פרוטה a fixed measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible answer: the משנה's value was for the Torah's time, but today any coin people call a פרוטה would do. אביי shows that sages in later generations still measured the פרוטה against the איסר. The two reports differ (1/8 vs 1/6), but both treat the פרוטה as a set measure, not 'any amount.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; brings up a possible answer in order to reject it
The generation of משה, the time the Torah was given
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Estimated or measured

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get stuck on the difference between 1/8 and 1/6 yet. אביי's point here is only that both reports give a fixed number. The גמרא explains the difference in steps 14 to 19.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: And if you will say: This applies only in the generation of משה,
but here it goes by what people consider it to be,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: But when רב דימי came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעֵר רַבִּי סִימַאי בְּדוֹרוֹ כַּמָּה הִיא פְּרוּטָה:
phrases.english: רבי סימאי measured in his generation how much a פרוטה is:
one-eighth of the Italian איסר,
and when רבין came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: רבי דוסתאי, רבי ינאי and רבי אושעיא
measured how much a פרוטה is:
one-sixth of the Italian איסר!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens אביי's challenge by blocking a possible way out
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible answer that the fixed value applied only in משה's time
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Sages in later generations also measured the פרוטה as a fixed fraction of the איסר.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the numbers in a ברייתא don't fit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the fixed value of one-eighth of an איסר. A ברייתא says two סלעים hold more than two thousand פרוטות, but by that measure they hold fewer than two thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: If so, is this what we learned: 'Go and count how many פרוטות are in two סלעים: more than two thousand'? Now there are not even two thousand, and it calls them more than two thousand?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף fights back. He shows that a ברייתא's count does not match a פרוטה worth one-eighth of an איסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two סלעים are 8 דינרים. A דינר is 24 איסרים, and an איסר is 8 פרוטות, so that comes to only 1,536 פרוטות. The ברייתא says 'more than two thousand,' which suggests a פרוטה is smaller than one-eighth of an איסר, perhaps not a fixed amount at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a problem that follows from the other side's view
Is this what we learned? Here it is said with surprise, pointing to a contradiction
A large silver coin worth 4 דינרים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי,
phrases.english: רב יוסף said to him: If so,
is this what we learned?
'Go and count how many פרוטות
are in two סלעים: more than two thousand.'
Now there are not even two thousand,
and it calls them more than two thousand?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דְּתָנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף counters אביי's proof
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a פרוטה is fixed at one-eighth of an איסר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At one-eighth of an איסר, two סלעים hold only 1,536 פרוטות, not more than 2,000 as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: An old man fixes the wording: close to two thousand
steps.stepSummary: An elderly scholar says that in his version the ברייתא reads 'close to two thousand,' not 'more than two thousand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man said to them: I learned it as 'close to two thousand.'
steps.whatsHappening: An old man answers רב יוסף's challenge by giving a different version of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא says 'close to two thousand,' then the number does not have to go over 2,000. The fixed value of one-eighth of an איסר can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain old man; an unnamed elderly scholar
Close to two thousand

phrases.english: A certain old man said to them:
I learned it as: 'close to two thousand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ הַהוּא סָבָא אֲנָא תְּנֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says more than 2,000, which clashes with one-eighth of an איסר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'close to two thousand,' so there is no clash.

steps.title: But 1,536 is not close to two thousand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the old man's version: 1,536 is still far from two thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, there are only one thousand five hundred thirty-six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the old man's answer. Even 'close to two thousand' seems like a stretch for 1,536.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 8 דינרים × 24 איסרים × 8 פרוטות = 1,536. That is almost 500 short of 2,000, so calling it 'close' still seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, after all; pushes back after an answer

phrases.english: In the end, one thousand five hundred
and thirty-six is all there are!
phrases.notes: That is 8 דינרים, times 24 איסרים per דינר, times 8 פרוטות per איסר.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף אַלְפָּא וַחֲמֵשׁ מְאָה וּתְלָתִין וְשִׁיתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the old man's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 1,536 is far from 2,000, so even 'close' does not fit.

steps.title: Past the halfway point counts as close
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since 1,536 is past the halfway mark between one thousand and two thousand, it can be called 'close to two thousand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it passes the half, it is called close to two thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the old man's wording. Once a number passes the midpoint (1,500), it is described as close to the next thousand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 1,536 is over 1,500, so it is nearer to 2,000 than to 1,000. That is enough to call it 'close to two thousand.' This saves the fixed value of one-eighth of an איסר.

keyTerms.meaning: From the half; past the halfway point

steps.whatToRemember: A פרוטה has a fixed value, not 'any amount.' The ברייתא's count of פרוטות in two סלעים fits one-eighth of an איסר once we read 'close to two thousand.'

phrases.english: Since it goes past the half,
phrases.notes: He means past 1,500, the midpoint between one thousand and two thousand.

phrases.english: it is called close to two thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקָא לְהוּ מִפַּלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the old man's version
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining how the wording is used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 1,536 is too far from 2,000 to be called close.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any number past the halfway point is called close to the next thousand.

steps.title: Back to the reports of רב דימי and רבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the two reports quoted earlier, to examine them on their own: רבי סימאי said one-eighth of an איסר, and the other sages said one-sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי סימאי measured in his generation how much a פרוטה is: one-eighth of the Italian איסר. And when רבין came, he said: רבי דוסתאי, רבי ינאי and רבי אושעיא measured how much a פרוטה is: one-sixth of the Italian איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the two reports so it can study them directly. This sets up the next question about why they differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier these reports were used only to prove that a פרוטה has a fixed value. Now the גמרא looks at the difference between them, 1/8 versus 1/6.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; the גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: The matter itself: When רב דימי came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעֵר רַבִּי סִימַאי בְּדוֹרוֹ כַּמָּה הִיא פְּרוּטָה –
phrases.english: רבי סימאי measured in his generation how much a פרוטה is:
one-eighth of the Italian איסר,
and when רבין came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעֲרוּ רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: רבי דוסתאי, רבי ינאי and רבי אושעיא measured
how much a פרוטה is:
one-sixth of the Italian איסר.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to statements first quoted in step 9 in order to study them directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two reports of the פרוטה's value: one-eighth or one-sixth of an Italian איסר.

steps.title: אביי asks: is this an argument between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי whether he and רבין are really disagreeing in the same way as an earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: Shall we say that you and רבין disagree about the same issue as these תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to suggest that the two reports match an older argument between תנאים. The גמרא quotes that argument in steps 16 and 17, and אביי finishes his question in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of seeing 1/8 and 1/6 as a simple clash in reports, אביי suggests the difference goes back to a known disagreement among תנאים. The ברייתא in steps 16 and 17 shows which תנאים he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Offers a suggestion that is often tested or rejected
A disagreement
תנאים, the sages of the משנה period

phrases.english: אביי said to רב דימי:
Shall we say that you and רבין
are disagreeing about the dispute of these תנאים,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי נֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what lies behind the two different reports
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 1/8 versus 1/6 difference between רב דימי and רבין follows an earlier dispute between תנאים

steps.title: The תנא קמא's coin chart: a פרוטה is one-eighth of an איסר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which the תנא קמא lists the coins from a silver דינר down to a פרוטה and finds that a פרוטה is one-eighth of an Italian איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the פרוטה the Sages spoke of is one-eighth of the Italian איסר. Six silver מעה make a דינר. A מעה is two פונדיון. A פונדיון is two איסר. An איסר is two מסמס. A מסמס is two קונטרונק. A קונטרונק is two פרוטות. So a פרוטה comes out to one-eighth of the Italian איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source behind אביי's question from the last step. The גמרא quotes the first opinion in the ברייתא, which works down the coin ladder and finds 8 פרוטות in one איסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Do the math: an איסר is 2 מסמס, which is 4 קונטרונק, which is 8 פרוטות. Going up the ladder, a דינר is 6 מעה, which is 12 פונדיון, which is 24 איסר, so a דינר holds 192 פרוטות. This one-eighth number matches what רבי סימאי said in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin, and the minimum value for קידושין
The Italian איסר, a small copper coin
A silver coin; six of them make a דינר
A coin worth half a מעה
A silver coin, also called a זוז

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: The פרוטה that the Sages spoke of
is one-eighth of the Italian איסר.
Six silver מעה make one דינר,
a מעה is two פונדיון,
a פונדיון is two איסר,
an איסר is two מסמס,
a מסמס is two קונטרונק,
a קונטרונק is two פרוטות.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא, פְּרוּטָה – אֶחָד מִשְּׁמֹנָה בָּאִיסָּר הָאִיטַלְקִי.
phrases.english: It turns out a פרוטה is one-eighth of the Italian איסר.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: פְּרוּטָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that אביי's question in step 15 refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a פרוטה is one-eighth of an Italian איסר (192 פרוטות to a דינר).

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's chart: a פרוטה is one-sixth of an איסר
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל divides the מעה differently and finds that a פרוטה is one-sixth of an Italian איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: three הדרס make a מעה, two הנץ make a הדרס, two שמין make a הנץ, and two פרוטות make a שמין. So a פרוטה comes out to one-sixth of the Italian איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion in the same ברייתא uses a different breakdown of the מעה and finds only 6 פרוטות in an איסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his count, a מעה is 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 24 פרוטות. A מעה is also 4 איסר (2 פונדיון, each worth 2 איסר), so each איסר is 6 פרוטות. This matches the one-sixth number the other sages gave in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth one-third of a מעה in his chart
'It turns out', introducing the result of a calculation

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Three הדרס make a מעה,
two הנץ make a הדרס,
two שמין make a הנץ,
two פרוטות make a שמין.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא, פְּרוּטָה – אֶחָד מִשִּׁשָּׁה בְּאִיסָּר הָאִיטַלְקִי.
phrases.english: It turns out a פרוטה is one-sixth of the Italian איסר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשָׁה הַדְרֵסִין לְמָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a פרוטה is one-sixth of an Italian איסר.

steps.title: אביי completes his question: does each אמורא follow a different תנא?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי whether he holds like the תנא קמא (one-eighth) and רבין holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (one-sixth).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that you, Master, hold like the תנא קמא, and רבין holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא has been quoted, אביי spells out his question. Are רב דימי and רבין simply repeating the old argument of the תנאים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's report of one-eighth lines up with the תנא קמא, and רבין's report of one-sixth lines up with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. אביי wants to know if that is truly the source of their difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say?', a suggestion the גמרא often goes on to reject
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
'Master', a respectful way of saying 'you'

phrases.english: Shall we say that the Master spoke like the first Tanna,
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is רב דימי himself, the one אביי is talking to.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבִין דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: and Ravin, who spoke like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּמָר אָמַר כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the two opinions in the ברייתא to the two reports, finishing the question opened in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are רב דימי and רבין disagreeing in the same way as the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?

steps.title: רב דימי: both follow the תנא קמא; the איסר's price changed
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that both he and רבין hold like the תנא קמא. The difference comes from the copper איסר going up or down in value against the silver דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Both I and רבין hold like the תנא קמא, and there is no difficulty. One statement is for when the איסר became expensive, and the other is for when it became cheap. When the איסר was expensive, 24 of them stood at one זוז. When it was cheap, 32 of them stood at one זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי rejects אביי's suggestion. He explains that the two numbers come from different market times, not from a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוטה stays fixed at 1/192 of a silver דינר (זוז). When the איסר was expensive, 24 made a זוז, so each איסר held 192 ÷ 24 = 8 פרוטות. When it was cheap, 32 made a זוז, so each איסר held only 192 ÷ 32 = 6 פרוטות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to', following someone's opinion
'And it is not difficult', the two statements don't really clash
Became expensive, went up in value
Became cheap, went down in value
A זוז, the same as a silver דינר

steps.whatToRemember: The פרוטה is measured against silver and never changes: 192 to a דינר. Only the copper איסר changes price, which is why it sometimes holds 8 פרוטות and sometimes 6.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the value of a פרוטה itself is changing. It is the איסר that goes up and down; the פרוטה stays the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין דִּידִי וּבֵין רָבִין
phrases.english: He said to him: Both I and Ravin
follow the first Tanna,
and it is not difficult:
this one is when the איסרים became expensive,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is רב דימי's own number, one-eighth.

phrases.english: that one is when the איסרים became cheap.
When the איסרים became expensive,
twenty-four stood at one זוז;
when they became cheap,
thirty-two stood at one זוז.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין דִּידִי וּבֵין רָבִין אַלִּיבָּא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by turning down the suggested link to the תנאים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both follow the תנא קמא; the gap between one-eighth and one-sixth comes from the איסר being worth 24 or 32 to the זוז at different times, while the פרוטה stays fixed against silver.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the פרוטה is pegged to silver, which is the true measure for the minimum value of קידושין.

steps.title: שמואל: betrothal with one date is valid out of concern
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a man is מקדש a woman with one date, she is מקודשת even where dates are very cheap, because the date may be worth a פרוטה in מדי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If he was מקדש her with a date, she is מקודשת even if a כור of dates sells for one דינר. We are concerned that it may be worth a פרוטה in מדי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. שמואל rules on קידושין done with an item worth less than a פרוטה here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כור is a huge amount, so one date here is worth far less than a פרוטה. Even so, שמואל worries that in a faraway place like מדי a single date may be worth a פרוטה. Because of that worry, we cannot treat the קידושין as nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He was מקדש her, made her his betrothed
A date (the fruit)
A very large measure of volume
'We are concerned', we take a possibility into account
Media, a distant land

steps.confusionAlert: The word חיישינן tells you the ruling rests on a worry, not on proof that the date is worth a פרוטה. Read מקודשת here as 'we must treat her as possibly betrothed.'

phrases.english: Shmuel said: If he betrothed her with a date,
even if a כור of dates stands at one דינר,
she is betrothed;
we are concerned that perhaps it is worth a פרוטה in מדי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קִידְּשָׁהּ בִּתְמָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the coin-value discussion and opens a new ruling about the פרוטה minimum for קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with a single date is taken seriously even where dates are very cheap, out of concern that the date is worth a פרוטה in מדי.

steps.title: The משנה says a פרוטה is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with the משנה where בית הלל say קידושין needs a פרוטה or something worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: בית הלל say a woman is betrothed with a פרוטה or with something worth a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל. The משנה sets a minimum of one פרוטה, so how can a date worth less than that work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל set a clear minimum: one פרוטה. שמואל seems to say an item worth less than a פרוטה here can still work. That looks like a direct clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? An opening used to challenge something
The school of הלל, whose ruling is followed in the משנה here
Something worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה of קידושין, at the start of the פרק.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
With a peruta or with something worth a peruta!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that קידושין with one date counts even where dates are cheap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires a full פרוטה, but שמואל allows an item worth less than a פרוטה in this place.

steps.title: Certain קידושין versus doubtful קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about certain קידושין. שמואל is only talking about doubtful קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a difficulty. This (the משנה) is about certain קידושין, and this (שמואל) is about doubtful קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה and שמואל are talking about two different levels of קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a full פרוטה, the קידושין is definitely valid, and that is the משנה's case. With less than a פרוטה, שמואל never said she is definitely married. He only said we are worried that she might be, because the item could be worth a פרוטה in מדי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
Certain, definite קידושין
Doubtful קידושין, where we are unsure if it took effect

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not say the woman is fully married. Doubtful קידושין means we treat her strictly because of the doubt. That is not the same as a definite marriage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference between certain and doubtful קידושין is the same answer the גמרא will use again for the bundle of rags.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This is about certain betrothal,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה of בית הלל.

phrases.english: and this is about doubtful betrothal.
phrases.notes: 'This' is שמואל's ruling about the date.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי וַדַּאי, הָא בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and the משנה seemed to disagree about the minimum value for קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה sets the minimum for certain קידושין. שמואל only creates a doubt.

steps.title: A man betroths with a bundle of rags
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא checked whether a bundle of rags was worth a פרוטה. If it was, the קידושין counts, and if not, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags. רב שימי בר חייא sat before רב and checked it: if it was worth a פרוטה, yes, she is betrothed; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. Before רב, they decided the קידושין by checking whether the rags were worth a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way they ruled sounds like a simple yes or no based on the local value. That seems to leave no room for שמואל's worry about the value in מדי. The גמרא is setting up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain man. This opens a story about a real case
A bundle of rags
Examines, checks

phrases.english: A certain man betrothed a woman
with a bundle of rags.
Rav Shimi bar Hiyya sat
before Rav
and examined it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – אִין,
phrases.english: if it is worth a peruta, yes (she is betrothed);
if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאקַדֵּישׁ בִּזְווֹדָא דְּאוּדְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that seems to clash with שמואל's ruling in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the קידושין counts depends on whether the rags are worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: What about שמואל's worry?
steps.stepSummary: If the rags are worth less than a פרוטה, is she really not betrothed at all? שמואל said we worry that she might be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not worth a פרוטה, is she not betrothed? But שמואל said: we are concerned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling in the rags case using שמואל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling said 'if not, no', which sounds like the קידושין is completely void. But שמואל said that even below a פרוטה we must worry about the value in מדי. So it looks like the ruling ignores שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we take the possibility seriously
But didn't he say? Used to raise a challenge from someone's statement

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לֵית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה לָא?
phrases.english: And if it is not worth a peruta, she is not betrothed?
But Shmuel said: we are concerned!
phrases.notes: The worry is that the item might be worth a פרוטה in מדי, from his ruling about the date.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה לָא? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the rags case that she is not betrothed if the rags are worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל holds that even below a פרוטה there is a doubt, so 'no' seems too simple.

steps.title: Again: certain versus doubtful
steps.stepSummary: The rags ruling is about certain קידושין. שמואל's worry is about doubtful קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a difficulty. This (the rags ruling) is about certain קידושין, and this (שמואל) is about doubtful קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ruling says 'if not, no', it means she is not certainly married. That still leaves room for שמואל's doubt. So the two do not clash.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This is about certain betrothal,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ruling in the rags case.

phrases.english: and this is about doubtful betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי וַדַּאי, הָא בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 the same way step 22 answered step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: certain קידושין versus doubtful קידושין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rags ruling seemed to reject שמואל's worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rags ruling only decides certain קידושין, so שמואל's doubt still stands.

steps.title: A man betroths with a blue stone
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא estimated whether a blue stone was worth a פרוטה. If it was, she is betrothed, and if not, she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man betrothed a woman with a blue stone. רב חסדא sat and estimated its value: if it was worth a פרוטה, yes; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, similar story, this time ruled by רב חסדא. It is setting up the same kind of question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the ruling is a simple yes or no based on whether the item is worth a פרוטה. The question is whether this ruling also leaves room for שמואל's doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A blue stone, a colored stone
Estimates, assesses the value

phrases.english: A certain man betrothed a woman
with a blue stone.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב חִסְדָּא וְקָא מְשַׁעֵר לַיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Hisda sat and estimated its value:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – אִין,
phrases.english: if it is worth a peruta, yes;
and if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאקַדֵּישׁ בְּאַבְנָא דְכוּחְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, built like the story in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא makes the קידושין depend on whether the stone is worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: Same challenge from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: If the stone is worth less than a פרוטה, is she really not betrothed? שמואל said we worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not worth a פרוטה, is she not betrothed? But שמואל said: we are concerned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same challenge from שמואל, this time against רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question uses the same words as step 24. Here, though, the גמרא will give a different answer.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לֵית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה לָא?
phrases.english: And if it is not worth a peruta, she is not betrothed?
But Shmuel said: we are concerned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵית בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה לָא? וְהָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that she is not betrothed if the stone is worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says that even below a פרוטה we must be concerned.

steps.title: רב חסדא disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא simply does not hold like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא does not agree with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of splitting the cases, the גמרא says רב חסדא really does disagree with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the גמרא does not say 'certain versus doubtful'. It admits that רב חסדא rejects שמואל's worry. For him, if the item is not worth a פרוטה, the קידושין does not take effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold this view, he disagrees

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the challenge from שמואל. For the משנה and the rags case, the גמרא says 'certain versus doubtful'. For רב חסדא, it says he disagrees with שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: Rav Hisda does not hold like Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 in a different way than steps 22 and 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement: the two אמוראים hold different views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רב חסדא also leaves room for שמואל's doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא disagrees with שמואל. Below a פרוטה, there is no קידושין at all.

steps.title: The mother says the stone was worth a פרוטה then
steps.stepSummary: A mother tells רב חסדא that on the day of the קידושין, the stone was worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother said to him: But on the day he betrothed her, it was worth a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. A mother objects to רב חסדא's ruling and claims the stone used to be worth more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stone was worth a פרוטה when it was given, then the קידושין should count even under רב חסדא's own view. Her claim pushes for the woman to be treated as married.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother
That day

phrases.english: His mother said to him (to Rav Hisda):
phrases.notes: The text just says 'his mother'. It seems to mean the mother of the man who gave the stone.

phrases.english: But on that day that he betrothed her,
it was worth a peruta!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the blue stone from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling based on the stone's present value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What should matter is the value on the day of the קידושין, and she claims it was a פרוטה then.

steps.title: Her word cannot forbid the woman to a later man
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that her claim does not have the power to forbid the woman to a man who betroths her later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: It is not in your power to forbid her to a later man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the mother's claim. Her saying so cannot make the woman forbidden to anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone is not worth a פרוטה now. The mother's statement about its past value is not enough to make the קידושין take effect. So if another man betroths the woman later, she is not forbidden to him because of her claim.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in your power, you are not believed for this
To a later one, a man who comes after

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא judges by the stone's value now. A later claim that it used to be worth a פרוטה is not believed enough to forbid the woman to another man.

phrases.english: He said to her:
It is not in your power
to forbid her to a later man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: לָאו כָּל כְּמִינָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב חסדא answers the mother's claim from step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not believed: her statement does not have the power to change the woman's status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her claim about the earlier value might make the קידושין count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her word cannot forbid the woman to a later man, so רב חסדא's ruling stands.
